mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer demand, measured by HOUST, leads to higher corporate earnings expectations and pushes S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns show no statistically significant correlation with HOUST in the same window (Pearson's r < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in employment, as reflected in PAYEMS, reduces labor market uncertainty and boosts investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 20-day backtest shows negative returns whenever PAYEMS increases >10% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below trend signals supply-side weakness that raises the cost of capital, depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day rolling returns show no significant negative correlation with INDPRO declines (Spearman's rho > -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 1% over 3 months, the S&P 500 exhibits negative forward returns over the next 20 days due to tightened financing conditions.
failure_condition: In rate hike periods, 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from the pre-hike period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both consumer (HOUST) and business (GDPC1) demand create a dual positive shock to earnings expectations, producing a significant positive S&P 500 forward return over 20 days when both proxies rise.
failure_condition: In windows where both proxies rise, 20-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% triggers a labor market tightening that accelerates equity valuation growth, yielding positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% in a month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are flat or negative during UNRATE < 4.5% episodes.

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 237 for 3 months), the Fed is expected to hold rates steady, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 237 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In low-inflation regimes, 20-day returns show no outperformance versus high-inflation regimes (robustness test).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls for two consecutive months, supply constraints raise input costs, which depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly lower than average during such episodes (Granger causality rejected).
